Mr Christopher de Souza
Lessons on Singapore surviving

The speaker recalls learning from his parents on an airbase that Singapore must survive, which is what GE2015 means to him.

  2. s00004Mr Christopher de Souza — Holland-Bukit Timahcontext

    One of the earliest lessons that I can remember I learnt was there on that airbase.

  3. s00005Mr Christopher de Souza — Holland-Bukit Timah

    I remember both my father and mother teaching me that, "You must ensure that Singapore survives." Madam, this is what GE2015 means for me – that Singapore will survive.

    The speaker calls for support of a strong security budget, opposing calls to halve the defence budget given Singapore's geopolitical situation.

    2. s03001Ms Indranee Rajah

      Our Courts, in interpreting the Constitution, have determined that this right to legal counsel is to be exercised within a reasonable time after arrest and not immediately after arrest.

    • Mr Liang Eng Hwa
    Singapore's past growth competitive advantages

    Singapore created competitive advantages through infrastructure, connectivity, FTAs, MNCs, pro-business policies and low taxes, but capacity constraints mean lower growth and price competition.

    1. s03014Mr Liang Eng Hwa — Holland-Bukit Timahcontext

      Not just because we do it cheaper than others but rather, we were able to create our own competitive advantages.

    2. s03015Mr Liang Eng Hwa — Holland-Bukit Timah

      We engineered strong growth in manufacturing and services by way of a whole-of-Government approach – building the necessary infrastructure ahead of demand – ports, airport, industrial spaces – continually developing international linkages and connectivity to facilitate trade and investments, free trade agreements (FTAs), multinational corporations (MNCs) with their international links, instituting pro-business policies, among others, our low tax regime, and ensuring that there are sufficient manpower resources for businesses, both local sourced and foreign sourced.

    4. s03017Mr Liang Eng Hwa — Holland-Bukit Timahcontext

      Continuing this way of growing our economy is still a viable option, particularly in areas of high value adding, and it remains a policy option.

    5. s03018Mr Liang Eng Hwa — Holland-Bukit Timah

      However, given the inherent constraints in our capacity, that would mean we have to settle for a much lower growth range going forward and are destined to always compete with the next cheaper player.

    6. s03019Mr Liang Eng Hwa — Holland-Bukit Timahcontext

      We will also be at the mercy of the volatile global demand cycles, which tends to impact us more as a small and open economy.

    7. s03020Mr Liang Eng Hwa — Holland-Bukit Timah

      So, just adding value and competing on prices has become less of a value proposition for us, especially so as our economy matures and that we are near the limits in terms of manpower growth and land spaces.

      I do not want to raise excitement prematurely but I will say now that in due course, when I appoint the Electoral Boundaries Review Committee, I will instruct it to reduce the average size of GRCs further, and to create more SMCs.

    3. s03833Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      In 1990, we passed legislation to make the President an elected office, so that he could act as a stabiliser in our political system.

    4. s03834Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      The President would exercise custodial powers over the spending of past Reserves and key appointments in the public service – the two vital areas which I talked about earlier.

    5. s03835Mr Lee Hsien Loongcontext

      He would be directly elected by the people in a national election, so as to have the mandate and moral authority to say "no" to the Government, should this become necessary.

    6. s03836Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      We also created a Council of Presidential Advisors (CPA) to assist and advise the President in carrying out his duties and exercising his powers.

    • Mr Lee Hsien Loong
    President's non-executive role

    The President has no executive or policymaking role, which remains with the elected Government commanding the majority in Parliament.

    1. s03843Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      By design, the President has no executive, policymaking role and this remains the prerogative of the elected Government commanding the majority in Parliament.

    • Mr Lee Hsien Loong
    President's blocking power limits

    The Constitution lets the President block certain Government actions in carved-out areas but not initiate or champion policies.

    1. s03849Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      The Constitution gives him power to block certain actions of the Government, in areas which are specifically carved out for him.

    2. s03850Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      But it does not give him the power to initiate policies or generally to champion policies.

    • Mr Lee Hsien Loong
    Constitutional Tribunal and NIRC framework

    A Constitutional Tribunal was created for the President to refer constitutional questions, and the NIRC framework was introduced as a spending rule.

    1. s03861Mr Lee Hsien Loongcontext

      We created a Constitutional Tribunal to which the President can refer Constitutional questions which arise for an opinion, especially if there is a disagreement between him and the Government.

    2. s03862Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      We introduced the Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) framework, a new spending rule to enable the Government to tap a stable and sustainable income from our Reserves.

    • Mr Lee Hsien Loong
    President's permission for past Reserves

    The Government sought the President's permission to use past Reserves to fund the Jobs Credit scheme and Special Risk-Sharing Initiative.

    1. s03866Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      The Government, therefore, sought the President's permission to use past Reserves to fund the Jobs Credit scheme and the Special Risk-Sharing Initiative.

    • Mr Lee Hsien Loong
    Review Elected President qualifying criteria

    The passage states that the qualifying criteria for the Elected President should first be reviewed.

    1. s03888Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      First, we should review the qualifying criteria for the Elected President.

    • Mr Lee Hsien Loong
    Pegging criteria at senior management

    The concept was to peg the criteria at people with senior management competence and experience for assessing financial proposals and appointments.

    1. s03892Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      The concept was to peg it at people with senior management competence and experience, because they have to assess and decide on financial proposals which will involve billions of dollars, and they must judge and decide to approve or reject appointments of people into posts which will involve running big organisations, making decisions, investing, managing and spending billions of dollars.

    • Mr Lee Hsien Loong
    Inflation and growing reserves oversight

    The passage notes inflation figures and that economic growth, spending, Reserves, and organisation complexity have grown, with the President holding a second key on bodies like MAS, Temasek, GIC, HDB and JTC.

    1. s03897Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      Just based on inflation alone, $100 million in 1990 would be equivalent to $158 million today.

    2. s03898Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      But it is much more than inflation, which is at issue, because over 25 years, our economy has grown, Government spending has gone up, Government Reserves have accumulated, the size and the complexity of the organisations which are subject to the second key of the President have grown many-fold.

    3. s03899Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      Apart from the key appointments in the Government, the President also has a second key on organisations like the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), Temasek Holdings, GIC, the Housing and Development Board (HDB), and JTC.

    • Mr Lee Hsien Loong
    Government Budget spending growth

    Government Budget spending rose from S$11 billion in 1990 to S$68 billion in 2015, six times more.

    1. s03906Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      Our Government spending, the Government Budget, has gone up from S$11 billion in 1990 to S$68 billion in 2015 − six times.

    • Mr Lee Hsien Loong
    Companies with $100 million capital

    A report noted about 1,200 registered companies with paid-up capital of $100 million or more in 2010, which the speaker says is 2,100.

    1. s03917Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      After the last election, he sent me a report and I quote from the report, paragraph 6.1 in the conclusion: "In the course of its work, the Presidential Elections Committee (PEC) noted that there were about 1,200 registered companies with a paid-up capital of $100 million or more in 2010." As I pointed out today, it is 2,100.

    • Mr Lee Hsien Loong
    Reviewing President qualifying criteria

    The speaker agrees with Mr Eddie Teo that the qualifying criteria for candidates to be President should be reviewed.

    1. s03921Mr Lee Hsien Loongcontext

      However, the smallest companies in Singapore with a paid-up capital of $100 million today would fall well short in both size and complexity.

    2. s03922Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      This is an issue that the Government may wish to review." I agree with Mr Eddie Teo that we should review the qualifying criteria for candidates to be President.

    • Mr Lee Hsien Loong
    CPA advice weight in decisions

    Over time, consideration should be given to whether the CPA's advice should count for more in the President's decisions.

    1. s03927Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      Over time, as the new institutions of the President and the CPA established themselves, we should consider if the CPA's advice should come to count for more in the decisions made by the President, so as to make our governance system more stable.

    • Mr Lee Hsien Loong
    CPA views in custodial powers

    The arrangement does not apply uniformly to the President's custodial powers in other areas, and study is needed on giving the CPA's views greater weight.

    1. s03942Mr Lee Hsien Loongcontext

      This applies to supply bills, it applies to key appointments, but this arrangement does not apply uniformly when the President exercises custodial powers in other areas.

    2. s03943Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      We should study if the CPA's views should be given greater weight in more areas and, if so, how this can be done.

    • Mr Lee Hsien Loong
    No Malay President since 1991

    Since the Elected President system took effect in 1991, there has not been a Malay President.

    1. s03947Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      Since we introduced the Elected President system and brought it into effect in 1991, we have not had a Malay President.

    • Mr Lee Hsien Loong
    Constitutional Commission on Presidency

    A Constitutional Commission chaired by Chief Justice Sundaresh Menon will study eligibility criteria, the CPA and periodic minority Presidents.

    1. s03950Mr Lee Hsien Loongcontext

      It is the same problem with Parliamentary Elections which led us to create GRCs to ensure a minimum representation of minority race Members in Parliament.

    2. s03951Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      I think we should consider a similar mechanism for Presidential Elections to ensure that minorities can be periodically elected if we have not had a particular minority as President for some time.

    3. s03952Mr Lee Hsien Loongcontext

      These are three broad areas to look into: (a) to bring the eligibility criteria up to date; (b) to strengthen the CPA; and (c) to ensure minority Presidents periodically.

    4. s03953Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      I will appoint a Constitutional Commission to study these issues and make recommendations.

    5. s03954Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      It will be chaired by Chief Justice Sundaresh Menon and include distinguished jurists, academics and corporate executives.

    6. s03955Mr Lee Hsien Loong

      The Commission will look into each of these issues, take views from the public and, in due course, it will recommend how we can improve the system – I hope by the third quarter of this year.

    • Mr Lee Hsien Loong · Dr Janil Puthucheary
    National Day Parade reserve commander

    The speaker was at the Padang as reserve commander for the PCF Marching Contingent of the National Day Parade.

    1. s03971Mr Lee Hsien Loongcontext

      That way, future Governments can work with future citizens of Singapore to achieve happiness, prosperity and progress for our people.

    2. s03972Dr Janil Puthucheary

      I was at the Padang as I had the privilege to be the reserve commander for the PCF Marching Contingent of the National Day Parade (NDP).

    • Dr Janil Puthucheary
    Punggol-Damai SG50 celebration

    The speaker rushed to his constituency for a Punggol-Damai Residents' Committee SG50 celebration attended by several hundred families.

    1. s04002Dr Janil Puthuchearycontext

      When I left the Padang later that evening, I had an extra spring in my step and a song in my heart.

    2. s04003Dr Janil Puthucheary

      I was rushing back to my constituency to join the Punggol-Damai Residents' Committee for an SG50 celebration.

    3. s04004Dr Janil Puthuchearycontext

      They had worked very hard for many weeks, decorating their estate, building a little kampong, putting up flags everywhere, some big, some small.

    4. s04005Dr Janil Puthucheary

      It was a great event, a huge event, with several hundred families having a great time.

    • Dr Janil Puthucheary
    Last song Majulah Singapura

    The last song was going to be "Majulah Singapura".

    1. s04009Dr Janil Puthucheary

      The last song, of course, was going to be "Majulah Singapura".

    • Dr Janil Puthucheary
    Boy singing out of time

    A young voice sang loudly and with gusto but out of time during the pause between the verses.

    1. s04016Dr Janil Puthuchearycontext

      Even worse, he did not know the timing.

    2. s04017Dr Janil Puthucheary

      So, as the first verse finished with "Berjaya Singapura", there is that pause into the short silence between the verses, you could hear this young voice with all his energy and gusto trying to sing, and trying loudly to sing but you could not really hear the words he was singing – completely out of time.

    • Dr Janil Puthucheary
    Race not asked about story

    The speaker says no one has asked about the race of the boys in his story, which is about Singaporeans regardless of race, language or religion.

    1. s04032Dr Janil Puthucheary

      In the Singapore of today, and in the six months I have been telling the story and boring my grassroots leaders with it, I have never even once been asked about the race of these boys – the soldiers and the little boy.

    3. s04034Dr Janil Puthucheary

      What does that say about the Singapore of today, that when I tell a story like this, it does not occur to anyone to ask, because it does not change the story – the story is about Singapore and Singaporeans, regardless of race, language or religion.

    • Dr Janil Puthucheary
    New citizen among boys

    The passage asks what happens if one of the boys in the story is a new citizen.

    1. s04049Dr Janil Puthuchearycontext

      And listening to my story, you understand this, you believe this, you embrace this.

    2. s04050Dr Janil Puthucheary

      But what if one of those boys is a new citizen?

    • Dr Janil Puthucheary
    Meaning of race language religion

    The passage asks what the phrase regardless of race, language or religion means.

    1. s04056Dr Janil Puthucheary

      What does it mean "Regardless of race, language or religion"?

    • Dr Janil Puthucheary
    Deeds words over Constitution pledge

    The passage states that dealing with fault lines of division depends less on the Constitution or pledge and more on deeds, actions and words.

    1. s04070Dr Janil Puthucheary

      How we deal with fault lines of division, depends less on the Constitution or our pledge and more on our deeds, our actions and our words – words that are said, words that are held back.

    • Dr Janil Puthucheary
    No second-class citizens

    The passage states the idea that there would be no second-class citizens and no child should grow up believing they are one.

    1. s04082Dr Janil Puthucheary

      The idea that in our country, there would be no second-class citizens.

    2. s04083Dr Janil Puthucheary

      No child in Singapore should grow up believing that they are a second-class citizen.

    • Dr Janil Puthucheary
    Religiously diverse racial harmony integration

    The passage states that after 50 years Singapore is one of the most religiously diverse countries, with celebrated racial harmony and integration.

    1. s04086Dr Janil Puthucheary

      After a short 50 years, we are one of the most religiously diverse countries in the world, and our racial harmony and integration are celebrated and something to be rightly proud of.

    • Dr Janil Puthucheary
    Deeds words for unity harmony

    The passage states that building a Singapore with unity of purpose depends most on deeds and words, spoken and held back.

    1. s04091Dr Janil Puthucheary

      If we are to build a Singapore with a unity of purpose, a nation that sees our diversity as strength, then it is our deeds and our words, spoken and held back that will matter most.

    3. s04093Dr Janil Puthuchearycontext

      We are a people who want unity and harmony and are prepared to put in the hard work to make this happen.

    4. s04094Dr Janil Puthucheary

      We are a people who understand that our diversity is our strength.

    • Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
    SkillsFuture and future skills

    SkillsFuture will prepare Singapore for the future economy through re-skilling, up-skilling, second-skilling, deep-skilling and multi-skilling.

    1. s04098Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar — Ang Mo Kio

      SkillsFuture will help to prepare us for the future economy through various skills, be it re-skilling, up-skilling, second-skilling, deep-skilling and even multi-skilling.

    • Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
    Entrepreneur schemes and SkillsFuture

    Government entrepreneur schemes exist, and SkillsFuture Credit and Earn and Learn can sharpen entrepreneurship and other career skills to enhance income and employment.

    1. s04104Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar — Ang Mo Kio

      Presently, there are many assistance schemes for entrepreneurs by the Government, like the Productivity and Innovation Credit (PIC), iSTART Accelerate and Catalyse Entrepreneurship (iSTART: ACE), and Capability Development Grant (CDG), among others.

    3. s04106Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar — Ang Mo Kio

      At the same time, the SkillsFuture initiatve – for instance, the SkillsFuture Credit and the SkillsFuture Earn and Learn – can help to improve and sharpen our skills in entrepreneurship as well as in other careers, with the aim of enhancing the income and employment opportunities for Singaporeans.

    • Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
    Undergraduates in general degree programmes

    The speaker urges MOE to help general degree undergraduates gain cross-discipline attachments, internships, multi-skilling or second-skilling for future employability.

    1. s04117Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar — Ang Mo Kiocontext

      However, at the same time, I am also concerned about one specific group of Singaporeans – our university undergraduates, particularly those in general degree programmes, who may not have industry-relevant training or skills.

    2. s04118Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar — Ang Mo Kio

      I would urge the MOE to look at how students in such programmes can benefit from cross-discipline attachments or internships, and opportunities for multi-skilling or second-skilling during the course of their undergraduate studies, so that they are more employable in future.

    • Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
    Reviewing academic stream categorisation

    The speaker urges MOE to review how students are categorised into Express, Normal (Academic) or Normal (Technical) streams.

    1. s04123Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar — Ang Mo Kio

      Specifically, I would urge MOE to review the way we categorise our students in schools into academic streams – Express or Normal (Academic) or Normal (Technical).

    • Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
    CCE lessons and SAP school admission

    The speaker proposes teaching CCE in common or form classes instead of Mother Tongue, and opening SAP schools to non-Chinese Mother Tongue students who take Chinese as a third language.

    1. s04144Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar — Ang Mo Kio

      First, in teaching Character and Citizenship Education (CCE) in schools, I propose that this be changed from being taught in Mother Tongue classes to common lessons or in the form classes at the primary school level.

    2. s04145Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar — Ang Mo Kio

      The rationale for teaching CCE in Mother Tongue classes may be to address racial issues or values more sensitively, but I believe that after 50 years of nation-building, our society is mature enough and sensible enough to discuss sensitive issues pertaining to character or citizenship openly and honestly, starting with our children who are even more race-blind.

    4. s04147Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar — Ang Mo Kio

      Second, I would like to once again propose that our Special Assistance Plan (SAP) schools be opened up to admit students who do not take Chinese as a Mother Tongue language but who meet the school's cut-off point for the PSLE.

    5. s04148Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar — Ang Mo Kio

      I would propose that as a requirement of admission, these students will have to take Chinese as a third language from Secondary 1 to Secondary 4.

    • Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
    Piloting enhanced SAP schools

    The speaker asks for SAP schools to be enhanced and their social environment enriched, and for MOE to pilot this in one or two SAP schools.

      I am asking for the SAP schools to be enhanced and for its social environment to be enriched.

    2. s04153Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar — Ang Mo Kio

      I am asking for MOE to pilot this in one or two SAP schools to see how it works out.

    4. s04174Dr Teo Ho Pin — Bukit Panjangcontext

    2. s04204Dr Teo Ho Pin — Bukit Panjang

    • Mr David Ong

    Unwed mothers get half the maternity leave, no Baby Bonus or Parenthood Tax Rebates, and limited housing access.

    • Mr Ng Chee Meng

    Evolving meritocracy and opportunities

    1. s04359Mr Ng Chee Mengcontext

    The Hidden Good movement

    • Mr Ng Chee Meng
    Youth movement and Singapore Heartbeat

    A youth movement on social media highlights simple good deeds, bringing forth the Singapore Heartbeat.

    2. s04391Mr Ng Chee Meng

    • Mr Ng Chee Meng
    Growing economy, defence, Singapore heart

    The speaker calls for growing the economy, defending the country and forging a strong Singapore heart.

    1. s04398Mr Ng Chee Mengcontext

      We must continue to think wisely with our head to grow our economy.

    2. s04399Mr Ng Chee Meng

      We must build our muscle to defend our country.

    3. s04400Mr Ng Chee Meng

      At the same time, I call on this House and fellow Singaporeans to forge a strong Singapore heart.

    • Mr Low Thia Khiang
    SkillsFuture and confident Singaporeans
